ownership: Captured operations retain parameter references and fixed staging/output tensors; they capture no KV arena or request-owned page metadata.
QKV outputs are consumed by attention before the next projection graph reuses their shared buffers.
Feed-forward output is consumed by the next attention/residual operations before its buffer is overwritten; the final norm returns a separate tensor.
Current synchronous same-stream runner sequencing provides the required ordering. Concurrent forwards or multiple live Engines are outside the supported contract.
Sequential Engine rebinding does not invalidate these stateless graphs; the graph test covers reuse with different arenas.
rounding: Graph buckets retain the exact batch geometry; no token padding or new fused/compiled arithmetic is introduced.
The captured functions are the original eager bound methods. No norm accumulator, softcap, attention scale, or dtype is changed.
Startup graph checks compare replay with eager output; nonzero changed-input H100 primitive checks and full actual-runner diagnostics passed according to coordinator.
reporting: This is CUDA graph capture, not torch.compile or native paged attention.
Capture/startup duration is excluded from steady-state timing but must be reported separately.
Eligibility is one query token per row with exact batches 1/2/4/8, including a possible one-token prefill chunk. The 4K/8K prefill benchmark cases remain eager.
Unsupported row counts or query widths fall back eagerly and increment shape_or_layout; decode timing at the four configured batches should have no such fallbacks.
Per-shape capture memory deltas share a private pool; they must not be summed as total retained graph memory.
Memory totals should come from actual worker allocation/reservation and peak statistics; graph close is explicit on the helper, and worker termination currently owns runner teardown.
